'''Ersan İlyasova''' (born 15 May 1987)<ref>{{cite web|title=Ersan Ilyasova Stats, Video, Bio, Profile|url=http://www.nba.com/playerfile/ersan_ilyasova/|work=NBA.com|access-date=18 July 2007}}</ref> is an Uzbek-born Turkish former professional [[basketball]] player. He played 13 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), including nine seasons for the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. He also played in his native Turkey and for [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]] in Spain.

==Professional career==

=== Yeşilyurt (2003–2004) ===
İlyasova played for Yeşilyurt in the Turkish second-division league during the 2003–04 season.

=== Ülkerspor (2004–2005) ===
İlyasova stepped up to the [[Turkish Basketball League]] for the 2004–05 season with [[Ülker G.S.K.|Ülkerspor]], averaging 4.5 points and 3.2 rebounds in eleven games.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ersan Ilyasova – Turkish Basketball League Player|url=https://www.tblstat.net/player/736/0405|work=TBLStat.net|access-date=18 July 2007}}</ref>

===Milwaukee Bucks (2005–2007)===
İlyasova was selected by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] with the 36th overall pick of the [[2005 NBA draft]]. In July 2005, he joined the Bucks for the 2005 [[NBA Summer League]]. On 22 August 2005, he signed with the Bucks. On 14 November 2005, he was assigned to the [[Tulsa 66ers]] of the [[NBA Development League]], an assignment that lasted the entire [[2005–06 NBA season|2005–06 season]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks send Ersan Ilyasova to D-League|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/ilyasova-d-league-111405.shtml|work=InsideHoops.com|date=14 November 2005|access-date=18 July 2007}}</ref> In 46 games for the 66ers, he averaged 12.5 points, 7.0 rebounds and 1.0 assists per game.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ersan Ilyasova D-League Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/nbdl/players/i/ilyaser01d.html|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=18 July 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150428095244/http://www.basketball-reference.com/nbdl/players/i/ilyaser01d.html|archive-date=28 April 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

İlyasova made his NBA debut for the Bucks on 1 November 2006 in a 105–97 win over the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks at Detroit Pistons Box Score, November 1, 2006|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/200611010DET.html|work=Basketball-Reference.com|date=1 November 2006|access-date=1 November 2006}}</ref> In 2006–07, he played 66 games for the Bucks, averaging 6.1 points and 2.9 rebounds per game. In June 2007, the Bucks tendered a qualifying offer to İlyasova to make him a restricted free agent.

===Barcelona (2007–2009)===
[[File:ErsanIlyasova.JPG|thumb|upright=0.7|left|İlyasova with Barcelona in 2009]]
On 18 July 2007, İlyasova signed a two-year deal with [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]] of the [[Liga ACB]].<ref>{{cite web|title=AXA FC Barcelona lands Ilyasova|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/14516/axa-fc-barcelona-lands-ilyasova|work=Euroleague.net|date=18 July 2007|access-date=18 July 2007}}</ref> In [[2008–09 ACB season|2009]], he won a championship with Barcelona.

===Return to Milwaukee (2009–2011)===
In July 2009, İlyasova signed a multi-year deal to return to the Milwaukee Bucks.<ref>{{cite web|title=BUCKS REACH AGREEMENT WITH ILYASOVA|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/news/ilyasova_signing_090723.html|work=NBA.com|date=23 July 2009|access-date=23 July 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090727091438/http://www.nba.com/bucks/news/ilyasova_signing_090723.html|archive-date=27 July 2009|url-status=dead}}</ref>

=== Anadolu Efes (2011) ===
On 3 August 2011, İlyasova signed with [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]] of the Turkish Basketball League for the duration of the [[2011 NBA lockout|NBA lockout]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Anadolu Efes officially announces Ersan Ilyasova|url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/turkey/87834/anadolu-efes-officially-announces-ersan-ilyasova.html|work=Sportando.com|date=3 August 2011|access-date=3 August 2011}}</ref>

=== Third stint with Milwaukee (2011–2015) ===
In December 2011, İlyasova returned to the Bucks following the conclusion of the lockout.

On 19 February 2012, İlyasova set new career highs with 29 points and 25 rebounds against the [[New Jersey Nets]], becoming just the third Bucks player in franchise history to record at least 25 points and 25 rebounds in a game, after [[Kareem Abdul-Jabbar]] (10 times) and [[Swen Nater]] (once). The feat had not been achieved for more than 35 years.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ersan Ilyasova, Bucks spoil Brook Lopez's season debut for Nets|url=http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=320219017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120220031550/http://scores.espn.go.com/nba/recap?gameId=320219017|url-status=dead|archive-date=February 20, 2012|work=ESPN.com|date=20 February 2012|access-date=20 February 2012}}</ref> He subsequently earned the Player of the Week award for his performances from March 5–11.

On 12 July 2012, İlyasova re-signed with the Bucks on a multi-year deal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bucks Re-Sign Ersan Ilyasova|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-re-sign-ersan-ilyasova-0|work=NBA.com|date=12 July 2012|access-date=12 July 2012}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Bucks re-sign forward Ersan Ilyasova|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/8161151|work=ESPN.com|date=12 July 2012|access-date=12 July 2012}}</ref>

On 27 March 2014, İlyasova was ruled out for the remainder of the 2013–14 season due to a right ankle injury.<ref>{{cite web|first=Ben|last=Golliver|title=Bucks' Ersan Ilyasova out for season with ankle injury|url=https://www.si.com/nba/point-forward/2014/03/27/ersan-ilyasova-ankle-injury-update-milwaukee-bucks|work=SI.com|date=27 March 2014|access-date=27 March 2014}}</ref>

On 26 March 2015, İlyasova scored a career-high 34 points in a 111–107 win over the Indiana Pacers.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ilyasova scores 34 points, Bucks beat Pacers 111-107|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150326/INDMIL/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|date=26 March 2015|access-date=26 March 2015}}</ref>

===Detroit Pistons (2015–2016)===
On 11 June 2015, İlyasova was traded to the [[Detroit Pistons]] in exchange for [[Caron Butler]] and [[Shawne Williams]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Pistons Acquire Forward Ersan Ilyasova From Milwaukee In Exchange For Caron Butler And Shawne Williams|url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/pistons-acquire-forward-ersan-ilyasova-milwaukee-exchange-caron-butler-and-shawne-williams|work=NBA.com|date=11 June 2015|access-date=11 June 2015}}</ref> The move reunited him with [[Brandon Jennings]], with whom he played in Milwaukee.<ref>{{cite web|first=Jason|last=Brunskowski|title=Jennings and Ilyasova reunited in Detroit|url=https://www.detroitbadboys.com/2015/6/12/8771505/nba-trades-ersan-ilyasova-brandon-jennings|website=DetroitBadBoys.com|date=12 June 2015|access-date=27 December 2018}}</ref> On 27 October he made his debut for the Pistons in a 106–94 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]], recording 16 points, seven rebounds, three assists and one block in 34 minutes.<ref>{{cite web|title=Pistons surprise Hawks on opening night, winning 106-94|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20151027/DETATL/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|date=27 October 2015|access-date=27 October 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151028011535/http://www.nba.com/games/20151027/DETATL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=28 October 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Orlando Magic (2016)===
On 16 February 2016, İlyasova was traded to the [[Orlando Magic]], along with [[Brandon Jennings]], in exchange for [[Tobias Harris]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Magic Acquire Jennings and Ilyasova From Pistons in Exchange for Harris|url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-acquire-jennings-and-ilyasova-pistons-exchange-harris|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=16 February 2016|access-date=16 February 2016}}</ref> The next day, he made his debut with the Magic in a 110–104 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]], recording 16 points, five rebounds, two assists and one steal in 23 minutes.<ref>{{cite web|title=Mavs set franchise best for 3s but lose to Magic in OT|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160219/DALORL/gameinfo.html|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=19 February 2016|access-date=19 February 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160219040122/http://www.nba.com/games/20160219/DALORL/gameinfo.html|archive-date=19 February 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Oklahoma City Thunder (2016)===
On 23 June 2016, İlyasova was traded, along with [[Victor Oladipo]] and the draft rights to [[Domantas Sabonis]], to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in exchange for [[Serge Ibaka]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Thunder Acquires Oladipo, Ilyasova and Draft Rights to Sabonis|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/acquisitions_160623|work=NBA.com|date=23 June 2016|access-date=3 July 2016}}</ref> He appeared in three games for the Thunder to begin the [[2016–17 Oklahoma City Thunder season|2016–17 season]].

===Philadelphia 76ers (2016–2017)===
On 1 November 2016, İlyasova was traded, along with a conditional first-round pick, to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in exchange for [[Jerami Grant]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2016-11-01 |title=Thunder acquire Jerami Grant from Sixers for Ersan Ilysavoa, draft pick |url=https://www.nba.com/news/oklahoma-city-thunder-philadelphia-76ers-trade-jerami-grant-ersan-ilyasova |access-date=2026-05-23 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref> He made his debut for the 76ers the next day, scoring an equal team-high 14 points on 5-for-12 shooting in a 109–93 loss to the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Batum breaks out, leads Hornets past 76ers 109-93|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899506|work=ESPN.com|date=2 November 2016|access-date=3 November 2016}}</ref> On 6 December he had season bests of 23 points and 17 rebounds in a 96–91 loss to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Gasol has 26 points, 12 boards to lead Grizzlies past Sixers|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899760|work=ESPN.com|date=6 December 2016|access-date=6 December 2016}}</ref> He had a second 23-point game on 8 December against the [[New Orleans Pelicans]], and a third 23-point game on 30 December against the [[Denver Nuggets]]—both resulting in wins.<ref>{{cite web|title=Ersan Ilyasova 2016-17 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/i/ilyaser01/gamelog/2017/|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=31 December 2016}}</ref> On 29 January 2017, he scored a season-high 31 points in a 121–108 loss to the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Butler, Lopez lead Bulls to 121-108 win over 76ers|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900137|work=ESPN.com|date=29 January 2017|access-date=30 January 2017}}</ref>

===Atlanta Hawks (2017–2018)===
On 22 February 2017, İlyasova was traded again, this time to the [[Atlanta Hawks]] in exchange for [[Tiago Splitter]], a protected 2017 second-round pick, and the option to swap a second-round pick.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Odum |first=Charles |date=2017-02-23 |title=Atlanta Hawks pick up Ersan Ilyasova from Philadelphia 76ers for Tiago Splitter, picks |url=https://www.nba.com/news/hawks-acquire-ilyasova-sixers-splitter-picks |access-date=2026-05-23 |website=NBA.com |language=en}}</ref>

On 21 July 2017, İlyasova re-signed with the Hawks.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hawks Re-Sign Ersan Ilyasova|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-re-sign-ersan-ilyasova|work=NBA.com|date=21 July 2017|access-date=23 May 2026|last=Wilson|first=J}}</ref> On 26 February 2018, he was waived by the Hawks.<ref>{{cite web|title=Hawks Waive Ersan Ilyasova|url=https://www.nba.com/hawks/news/hawks-waive-ersan-ilyasova|work=NBA.com|date=26 February 2018|access-date=23 May 2026|last=Finberg|first=Annie}}</ref>

===Return to Philadelphia (2018)===
On 28 February 2018, İlyasova signed with the [[Philadelphia 76ers]], returning to the franchise for a second stint.<ref>{{cite web|title=Philadelphia 76ers Sign Forward Ersan Ilyasova|url=https://www.nba.com/sixers/philadelphia-76ers-sign-forward-ersan-ilyasova|work=NBA.com|date=28 February 2018|access-date=23 May 2026|last=Disdier|first=Ryan}}</ref>

===Fourth stint with Milwaukee (2018–2020)===
On 16 July 2018, İlyasova signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], returning to the franchise for a fourth stint.<ref>{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign Ersan Ilyasova|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/release/milwaukee-bucks-sign-ersan-ilyasova|work=NBA.com|date=16 July 2018|access-date=16 July 2018}}</ref> On 16 December 2018, he sustained a fractured nose during practice, which required surgery.<ref>{{cite web|title=Medical Update on Ersan Ilyasova|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/medical-update-ersan-ilyasova|work=NBA.com|date=21 December 2018|access-date=26 December 2018}}</ref>

On 19 November 2020, İlyasova was waived by Milwaukee.<ref>{{cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks Requested Waivers On Ersan Ilyasova|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/milwaukee-bucks-requested-waivers-ersan-ilyasova|work=NBA.com|date=19 November 2020|access-date=19 November 2020}}</ref>

===Utah Jazz (2021)===
On 11 March 2021, İlyasova signed with the [[Utah Jazz]] for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Utah Jazz sign Ersan Ilyasova|url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/utah-jazz-sign-ersan-ilyasova|work=NBA.com|date=10 March 2021|access-date=10 March 2021}}</ref> On 17 April, İlyasova logged a season-high 20 points on 7-for-11 field goal shooting and 6 of 8 from three, in addition to five rebounds, four steals and two blocks across 31 minutes in a 115–127 overtime loss to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Jazz's Ersan Ilyasova: Scores season-high 20 points|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/jazzs-ersan-ilyasova-scores-season-high-20-points/|website=CBSSports.com|date=17 April 2021|access-date=22 April 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=Lakers hold off NBA-leading Jazz 127-115 in OT|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401307651|website=ESPN.com|date=17 April 2021|access-date=22 April 2021}}</ref>

On 22 December 2021, İlyasova signed a 10-day contract with the [[Chicago Bulls]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Bulls Sign Ersan Ilyasova Via Hardship Exception|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2021/12/bulls-to-sign-ersan-ilyasova-via-hardship-exception.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=22 December 2021|access-date=22 December 2021}}</ref> İlyasova entered the NBA's health and safety protocols on December 28, and did not play for the team before his contract expired.

==National team career==
[[File:Savanović & İlyasova.jpg|thumb|271x271px|İlyasova (right) with Turkey in September 2010]]
Before playing for the senior [[Turkey national basketball team]], İlyasova was named the MVP of the [[2006 FIBA Europe Under-20 Championship]], after leading Turkey's junior national team to a silver medal in [[İzmir]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Luis|last=Fernández|title=A Look Back At The U-20 European Championships (Part Two)|url=http://www.draftexpress.com/article/A-Look-Back-At-The-U-20-European-Championships--Part-Two--1452/|work=DraftExpress.com|date=22 September 2006|access-date=22 September 2006|archive-date=September 8, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140908092138/http://www.draftexpress.com/article/A-Look-Back-At-The-U-20-European-Championships--Part-Two--1452/|url-status=dead}}</ref> İlyasova has since represented Turkey at the [[2006 FIBA World Championship]], [[EuroBasket 2007]], [[EuroBasket 2009]], [[2010 FIBA World Championship]], [[EuroBasket 2011]], [[EuroBasket 2013]] and [[EuroBasket 2015]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Ersan Ilyasova profile, EuroBasket 2015 - FIBA.COM|url=https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/43590/sid/9322/tid/376/_/2015_EuroBasket/index.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161231170647/https://archive.fiba.com/pages/eng/fa/player/p/pid/43590/sid/9322/tid/376/_/2015_EuroBasket/index.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=December 31, 2016|access-date=22 January 2017}}</ref>

==Personal life==
İlyasova is the son of [[Crimean Tatars|Crimean Tatar]] parents Anvar and Iraliye İlyasova.<ref>{{cite web|title=Life history of Crimean Tatar basketball player|url=http://qha.com.ua/en/sport/life-history-of-crimean-tatar-basketball-player/55452/|work=QHA.com.ua|date=23 September 2009|access-date=23 September 2009|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160521122953/http://qha.com.ua/en/sport/life-history-of-crimean-tatar-basketball-player/55452/|archive-date=21 May 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref> He is married to Julia, who was born in [[Belarus]]. They have two daughters, Catherine and Xenia, and one son, Nikita, all born in [[Milwaukee]].<ref name="rferl.org">{{cite news|title=Is Ilyasova A Turkish Name?|newspaper=Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty |date=July 13, 2012 |url=https://www.rferl.org/a/ilyasova-ilyasov-a-basketball-player-from-turkey-uzbekistan/24644497.html|access-date=22 January 2017}}</ref> İlyasova is Muslim.<ref>{{cite web|first=Marc J.|last=Spears|title=Being Muslim in the NBA|url=https://andscape.com/features/being-muslim-in-the-nba/|website=[[Andscape]]|date=17 October 2017|access-date=10 April 2021}}</ref>

===Citizenship and age===
Since the 2003 Turkish Junior Basketball Championship held in [[Konya]], there has been some controversy to İlyasova's age and national origin.<ref>{{cite web|title=SPORTS - Ulker implicated in Ilyasova scandal|url=http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/Default.aspx?pageID=438&n=ulker-implicated-in-ilyasova-scandal-2003-06-13|access-date=22 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170202010845/http://www.hurriyetdailynews.com/Default.aspx?pageID=438&n=ulker-implicated-in-ilyasova-scandal-2003-06-13|archive-date=2 February 2017|url-status=dead|df=dmy-all}}</ref> The controversy is fueled by the claim that a man named Arsen Ilyasov, born in 1984 in [[Bukhara]], [[Uzbekistan]], entered Turkey as an 18-year-old on 7 August 2002 and was never heard from again, while on 19 September 2002, a man named Semsettin Bulut claimed to have forgotten to register the birth of his now 15-year-old son, and did so as Ersan İlyasova, a Turkish citizen.<ref>{{cite web|title=DraftExpress: Ersan Ilyasova, the Turkish pearl|url=http://www.draftexpress.com/article/Ersan-Ilyasova-the-Turkish-pearl-82/|website=DraftExpress.com|access-date=22 January 2017|archive-date=December 1, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181201093115/http://www.draftexpress.com/article/Ersan-Ilyasova-the-Turkish-pearl-82/|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|title=The Don Draper of the NBA: Does Ersan İlyasova Really Exist?|url=https://thescorecrow.com/2019/05/31/the-don-draper-of-the-nba-does-ersan-ilyasova-really-exist/|website=The Scorecrow|date=31 May 2019|access-date=12 March 2021}}</ref> This claim, that İlyasova is actually Ilyasov and should be an Uzbek player, was officially put forth by the [[Uzbekistan Basketball Federation]] in a grievance, but [[FIBA]] ruled in the [[Turkish Basketball Federation]]'s favor.<ref name="rferl.org"/> While this controversy was brewing, [[ESPN]]'s [[Chad Ford]] referred to Ilyasova as "The 17-year-old forward from Uzbekistan is widely considered the best prospect to ever come out of Turkey."<ref>{{cite web|title=Ford: Turkey, Day One|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/columns/story?id=2052155&columnist=ford_chad|website=ESPN.com|date=5 May 2005|access-date=22 January 2017|last=Ford|first=Chad|url-status=dead|author-link=Chad Ford}}</ref> Other biographies, while not claiming an Uzbek birth, still maintain a 1984 birth year.<ref>{{cite web|title=Life history of Crimean Tatar basketball player|url=http://qha.com.ua/en/sport/life-history-of-crimean-tatar-basketball-player/55452/|access-date=22 January 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160609202531/http://qha.com.ua/en/sport/life-history-of-crimean-tatar-basketball-player/55452/|archive-date=9 June
